quests.title: The Grizzly Problem
quests.description: Bears do not come down to the water to watch a guard post.
quests.accept_text:
Bears keep to the trees. That is not a preference, it is what a bear IS - it wants cover and distance and no part of whatever we are doing.

These ones come down to the lake and stand in the open and watch this post. Not pacing. Not feeding. Standing, facing us, for as long as it suits them, and then going back up.

I have held Maestra's Post for eleven years and I have never once been watched by something that could not tell me why.

Put the boldest of them down before one of them walks into Astranaar's market and we find out what the next stage of this is.
quests.turn_in_text:
The lake shore's empty and nothing came down to the water today.

I'd be more relieved if I thought we'd solved it. We've removed the ones brave enough to come and look at us - that isn't the same as removing the reason they wanted to.

quests.title: Bark and Sap
quests.description: The wards are cracking, and heartwood is the only thing that holds one.
quests.accept_text:
Look at the posts. Go on - the carved ones at the corners. See the splits running with the grain?

Those are the wards, and they are the only reason this post sleeps at night. Heartwood holds a ward the way nothing I can requisition does. I have tried iron, I have tried stone, and I have tried asking Astranaar nicely, which was the least effective of the three.

The timberlings in Silverwind Vale carry it in their chests.

And before you ask me to be gentle about it - they came through my fence line last spring and they were not gentle with it, and I have a very long memory for fences.
quests.turn_in_text:
[She runs a thumb along the fresh grain.]

That's good wood. That'll hold a season, maybe two.

I'd rather be carving these because the old ones wore out than because something's been testing them. That's twice now this week I've wanted a different reason for a job.

quests.title: Ursal the Mauler
quests.description: With the totems dealt with, the Sentinels finally know where he lairs.
quests.accept_text:
Shalasyr sends word the totems are done. Good. Then whatever was feeding the Highland bears has stopped, and Ursal has nothing left driving him but his own temper - which, to be fair to him, has always been considerable.

He's the biggest of them and he's the one herding the others down toward the lake. That's been the shape of it all along: he moves, they move.

Go and finish it.

And do something for me. Before you do it, get a proper look at his eyes, and then come back and tell me honestly whether they were a bear's. I have asked three people that question and every one of them changed the subject.
quests.turn_in_text:
[She listens to your answer and does not react for a while.]

Thank you for saying it plainly.

Then he was being ridden, at the end, and he had been for a long time, and every one of those bears we put down at the shore was somebody else's hand moving. I'll carry that. It's better than not knowing.

quests.title: The Scout's Report
quests.description: Two scouts went up the ridge road nine days ago. Neither has reported.
quests.accept_text:
Two of mine went up the ridge road toward the Ragged Highlands nine days ago.

They are good. I want that understood before anything else, because the first thing anyone says is that scouts go missing and I will not have theirs be the generation that gets shrugged at. They are careful, they are experienced, and I would have heard from them by now if there were anything at all to hear.

Retrace their route. All of it, as far as the Highlands themselves.

I don't need heroics and I don't want a rescue attempt. I need to know the point on that road where it stops being safe, because at the moment I am sending people past it without knowing where it is.
quests.turn_in_text:
[Shalasyr marks the place on her own map and sits looking at it.]

That far. They got that far.

So the road is safe right up until it is extremely not, with no warning in between. That is the worst possible answer and it is the one I needed.

quests.title: What Turned the Furbolg
quests.description: Furbolg and Sentinels shared this forest for centuries without blood.
quests.accept_text:
I want to tell you something about the furbolg before you go up that ridge, because it matters and because nobody your age was taught it.

We have shared this forest with them for a very long time. Not an alliance - we were never that formal about it. We simply both lived here and both knew where the other's ground was, and in all that time there was not a drop of blood between us worth recording.

Now the ravagers hold the ridge and they attack anything that crosses it. Anything. They have stopped distinguishing.

Something has changed them, and I have to get scouts in there to find out what. Thin the ravagers so that becomes possible - and while you're among them, LOOK at them. Properly. You'll see what I mean and I'd rather you saw it than took my word.
quests.turn_in_text:
You saw it too, then. The eyes.

I've had that reported three times and dismissed it twice, because a Sentinel commander who starts talking about what she saw in an animal's eyes gets listened to differently afterwards.

Three is enough. I'm acting on it.

quests.title: The Shaman's Totems
quests.description: The ravagers are being driven from behind.
quests.accept_text:
The ravagers aren't the cause. I've been certain of that since the second report and now I can prove it, which is a different thing.

They're being driven from behind. The shamans plant totems in the dens, and the madness is always worst where the totems are thickest - not where the fighting is, not at the ridge, in the DENS, at the carvings.

Bring me some of those totems out.

And carry them in cloth. I mean that as an order rather than advice: I will not have you holding one of those bare-handed across half a forest to spare yourself the trouble of a wrapping.
quests.turn_in_text:
[She unwraps one with the cloth still between it and her hand, looks, and covers it again.]

That carving is not furbolg work. I don't know whose it is. I know whose it isn't.

Somebody walked into those dens and gave them this. That changes the question from what happened to the furbolg into who did it to them.

quests.title: Keeper Rustveil
quests.description: The Grove's guardian has turned against the forest he watched.
quests.accept_text:
Rustveil kept the Moonwhisper Grove before Astranaar had walls. Longer than that - before there was anyone here to need walls.

He taught me my first song. I was small enough that he had to bend down to it, and he was patient in a way that nothing that old has any reason to be.

Something has turned him against the forest he watched. I have been to see for myself and I will not describe it to you, partly to spare you and mostly to spare me.

I am asking you to put him down. I'm asking it knowing exactly what I'm asking and I will not dress it up as mercy or duty.

Do it quickly. If anything in him can still know what's happening, I don't want him knowing it for long.
quests.turn_in_text:
[Pennarin does not ask for any details.]

Quickly. Good.

The Grove will choose another keeper eventually. They always do - that's what a grove is, it outlasts whoever is minding it. I'll be glad of that in a year or so.

Today I would like to be left alone, and I would like you to know that is not ingratitude.

quests.title: Lights in the Grove
quests.description: The Grove's own lanterns are dimming.
quests.accept_text:
The wisps are the Grove's lanterns. That isn't poetry - that is their function and it is why the Grove is lit at all.

They're old. Older than the trees in some cases, and there is an argument, which I happen to believe, that they remember who planted this place.

They're flickering. Not dying out - flickering, the way a lamp does when something is wrong with the fuel rather than the wick, and I want the healers to have something to work from before it becomes the other thing.

Bring me what falls from them as they fade. And listen to me carefully: do not take a mote that has not fallen. Not one. I will know, and so will the Grove, and I am genuinely unsure which of us would be worse about it.
quests.turn_in_text:
[She holds a vial up and watches it pulse.]

All fallen. Thank you - and I did check, and I'd have thought less of myself for checking if I'd found you'd done it properly and never said.

The healers can work with this. Whatever's in the Grove, it's in the light first.

quests.title: What Was Left Behind
quests.description: A silver locket, taken by a nightsaber on the Night Run.
quests.accept_text:
I know how this sounds. I came off the east coast with a wagon and I lost the wagon, and what I'm asking a stranger to go and find is a piece of jewellery.

It's only silver. It's a painted picture, badly painted, by somebody in a market who charged too much.

It is the only picture of my sister that exists.

The wagon went over on the Night Run and a cat had it out of the box before I was back on my feet. I'm not asking for the rest - the rest was pots and clothes and I have made my peace with pots.

Just the locket. Please.
quests.turn_in_text:
[Thessaly opens it and looks at it for a long moment before she closes it again.]

That's her. That's a terrible likeness and that's her.

Thank you. I've spent three weeks telling myself it was only silver and I'd very nearly convinced me.

quests.title: Thinning the Stalkers
quests.description: There will be other wagons on that road.
quests.accept_text:
I keep seeing their eyes. When I close mine - the cats, in the dark, around the wagon while we were still getting out from under it.

I'm not going to pretend this is about my locket. You've already brought that back and I'm not owed anything else.

It's that there will be another family on that road next week. The Night Run is the only way through for anyone coming off the coast, and they'll be doing exactly what we did, at night, because that's when you're told it's safest.

Thin the stalkers before the next wagon tries it.

I'll sleep better. I think rather a lot of people will, and most of them will never know there was anything to sleep badly about, which seems to me the best possible outcome.
quests.turn_in_text: Seven. I'll tell the next wagon driver. He will pretend not to cry, and then he'll buy you a drink.

quests.title: Burning Blade Scouts
quests.description: Kill the scouts and the ritual circles cannot hide.
quests.accept_text:
Cultists poke about the Wastes like rats in a cellar, and like rats they are only interesting for what they lead you to.

The Burning Blade are putting up ritual circles out there. I can't find them - the Wastes are big and a circle is small and these people are not stupid about where they put them.

But I don't need to find the circles. I need to find the GUARDS, and guards stand near the thing they're guarding, which is the single most reliable fact in the practice of war.

Kill their scouts along the Wastes' edge. Wherever you have to kill a lot of them in one place, that is a circle, and then I can finish my map.
quests.turn_in_text: Eight. They guard more than I thought. I'll mark it on the map and show Vashj. You have the hands for this. I hope you have the stomach, too.

quests.title: The Charred Pack
quests.description: A wolf runs from fire. These come out of it.
quests.accept_text:
Used to be, a wolf ran from a fire. You could set a line and the whole forest would go the other way and that was something you could rely on.

These come out of the burn like they're from it. Straight through the black stretch at a dead run, into the open, at a line of armed orcs.

They've had two of my patrols bleeding and they've had the outpost's livestock, and I'll be honest with you that I mind the patrols more but the quartermaster minds the livestock.

Thin the pack. And while you're in there, find me whatever's making them burn-mad, because a wolf doesn't decide to do this on its own any more than it decides to walk into a fire.
quests.turn_in_text: Nine, and not a wolf among them behaved like a wolf. I owe you a drink and an apology to the dead ones. Nothing in the world should look at fire and stay.

quests.title: The Imp's Hoard
quests.description: They stack what they steal. It is not a nest.
quests.accept_text:
Hinges. Buckles. A strip of my own mess-tent canvas, cut square.

The imps carry off the dumbest things out of this outpost and they stack them in the dirt out in the Wastes, and I have been going out there to look at the stacks, which I'd rather you didn't mention to the War Mage.

Here's the thing. It isn't a nest. I've seen nests and I've seen hoards and this is neither - it's ARRANGED, the same way every time, and a thief doesn't arrange.

I think it's a message and I think nobody told us how to read it.

Bring me scraps off them. Enough that I can lay it out the way they do and look at the whole of it at once.
quests.turn_in_text: That's the hinge off my own tent flap. Right. The mess-tent has to stay up and the imps have to stay out. Thank you. Don't tell Sergeant Krull it was imps. He'll ask me why we couldn't stop them.

quests.title: Disrupting the Ritual
quests.description: They have been singing for three nights. It is not a welcome.
quests.accept_text:
The satyrs at Satyr's Throne have been singing for three nights.

I have interrogated a great many things in this forest and I have learned their songs the way you learn any language - by listening to it being used for ordinary purposes until the unusual ones stand out.

That is not a song of welcome. It is not a song of mourning either, which was my second guess and which I would have preferred.

It's preparation. Something is being made ready at the Throne and the tricksters are leading the chant, which means the tricksters are the part that has to be carried.

Remove them, and the song has nothing to carry it, and whatever is being prepared stays unprepared a while longer.
quests.turn_in_text: The chant has stopped. For tonight, anyway. You did well. Whoever commands them will be furious. I'd like to meet him on my terms.

quests.title: Lord Malgan
quests.description: A tyrant who loses a ritual has two choices.
quests.accept_text:
A tyrant who loses a ritual has two choices open to him. Try again, or die trying.

I have conducted enough interrogations to know which one Malgan will pick, and I have no intention of letting him get far enough into it to find out whether I'm right.

He holds the Throne by fear now rather than by strength. That is not the same thing and the satyrs under him know it even if he doesn't - you can hear it in how they move when he's in the open.

So I'll make the choice for him. He's at the Throne. Go and take it away from him.
quests.turn_in_text:
The Throne's empty and the satyrs have gone into the trees in every direction at once.

That's what fear buys you. Strength holds when the commander falls. Fear just stops.

quests.title: Voices from the Barrow
quests.description: Something under the Barrow is listening.
quests.accept_text:
Something under the Barrow is listening, and the acolytes are the ones doing the talking.

They go out at night and they whisper to the buried dead. Not chanting - whispering, the way you'd talk to somebody through a door, and you can stand on the mound and hear the shape of it without catching a word.

I don't know what's down there. I want to be extremely clear that I do not intend to find out by letting the conversation continue until it answers.

Silence the acolytes. Whatever is under that mound can go back to being a thing nobody has spoken to in a thousand years.
quests.turn_in_text: Quiet. Good. I felt it go quiet from the walls. Whatever was down there has lost its mouthpieces, for now.

quests.title: The Twilight Overseer
quests.description: Every cult has someone who is not a believer.
quests.accept_text:
Every cult has somebody in it who is not a believer. Only a boss.

You can pick him out at a distance if you know what to look for: he is the one who doesn't look up during the important part. The acolytes were whispering FOR somebody, and it was him.

Kill him and the rest scatter - or they come for you, which is a better fight than the one we'll be having if whatever is under that Barrow learns to speak for itself.

I would rather fight a hundred frightened cultists than one patient thing underground with a voice.
quests.turn_in_text: I can feel the Barrow settling. Well done. Now we only have to worry about everything else.

quests.title: The Emissary's Demand
quests.description: It arrived with terms.
quests.accept_text:
It arrived with terms.

It has been standing in the Wastes for two days waiting for somebody of appropriate rank to come out and receive them, and in that time three of my scouts have gone close enough to hear the opening and come back changed in ways I am still assessing.

I do not read the terms of things that stand in fire. There is no version of this where we hear it out and come away with more than we started with - that is what an emissary IS, it is a creature whose entire function is to make the next thing sound reasonable.

Cut it off before it finishes a sentence. Preferably the first one.
quests.turn_in_text: It was still talking when you reached it? Of course. They always are. I'll burn what's left of the terms. Thank you.

quests.title: Troubled Water
quests.description: They have always sung to us. Lately they sing and drag.
quests.accept_text:
The naiads have sung to us from Elune'ara for as long as there have been Sentinels on this shore. That is not a problem to be solved, it is simply what the lake does.

Lately they sing and then they DRAG. Two of my fishing party went in last week and came out, and one of them will not go near the water again, and she is not a woman who frightens.

I will not stand here and say that Lake Elune'ara is a danger. Elune help me, I will not say that out loud about this water.

I will say that some of its daughters are. Settle them, by the only means they've left anybody.
quests.turn_in_text:
[Maestra looks at the lake for a while.]

It's quiet. The singing's stopped on the near shore entirely.

I find I don't like that either. I have listened to that water sing my whole posting and I would not have chosen silence as the fix.

quests.title: Eyes on the Night Run
quests.description: Maestra is tired of not knowing.
quests.accept_text:
Eltharaen keeps asking me what's on the Night Run. He asks it in that patient way he has, as though I've simply not got round to finding out.

And I keep telling him I don't know, and every time I say it I like myself a little less.

The wagons die on that road. That's the extent of our intelligence - that's what I have to send up to Astranaar, that wagons die there, which anyone could have told me from the wreckage.

Walk it. End to end, all of it.

And tell me what that road looks like to someone who isn't afraid of it, because I am no longer certain I can see it clearly.
quests.turn_in_text: Wraith-light on the old tree line, you say? Then it's worse than the cats. I'll send for Eltharaen. And I'll find you more work.

quests.title: The Wraith's Toll
quests.description: The dead of the Run don't want revenge. They want company.
quests.accept_text:
Now I know what's on it, I can tell you what's wrong with it.

The dead of the Night Run don't want revenge. People assume they do, because people assume a hostile dead thing must have a grievance, and it makes the road easier to think about.

They want company. That's all. Every wagon that goes down that road is a crowd of warm people passing through a place where something is extremely alone, and they take a toll because taking is the only way they know to ask.

Understanding it doesn't help the carters. End the ones on the road, and the rest might remember they were people and settle.
quests.turn_in_text:
Road's open. There's a wagon due through from the coast tomorrow and I'm going to let it go.

First time in four months I've signed off on that without feeling like I was spending someone.

quests.title: Webs on the Trade Road
quests.description: He does not enjoy asking. He is also not a fool.
quests.accept_text:
I do not enjoy asking this of you, and I'd rather say that at the front than have it sit between us for the whole conversation.

My people are stretched from the coast to the Highlands. You are here. And the forest spiders on the trade road do not care in the slightest whose wagons they take - they have had Sentinel supply and they have had Horde supply and I understand they took a goblin caravan last month, which is the only part of this I've enjoyed.

So: clear the road.

And I will remember that it was asked and that it was answered. That's not nothing. In this forest, that has lately been most of what we have.
quests.turn_in_text: Nine. The road is clear. I will say this plainly: I did not expect to thank a Horde blade today. I find that I do.

quests.title: A Quiet Grove
quests.description: They answer when she sings. They have not answered in a week.
quests.accept_text:
The dryads answer when I sing. That is not a courtesy and it is not training - it is simply how it has always worked here, for as long as there has been a Grove to sing in.

They have not answered for a week.

I have been down there every evening. I have sung the calls they answer, and the old calls my teacher used before me, and last night I sang one I am not supposed to use outside of need. Nothing.

The corruption is in them now. It will not leave on its own and it will not leave because I ask it to; I have established both of those at some cost to my dignity.

I am sorry to ask you to release them. I am sorrier that I cannot do it myself without my voice being the last thing they hear.
quests.turn_in_text: The grove is a little less loud. I hope they're at peace. I hope the grove forgives me. Rustveil is next, I'm afraid.

quests.title: Marks on the Water
quests.description: Eleven nights of ripples that do not follow the wind.
quests.accept_text:
I keep a ledger of this lake's moods. It is not a poetic exercise - the Moon Guard have kept one here for generations and the entries are mostly about weather.

I have counted the ripples from the tower for eleven nights running.

They do not follow the wind. Not once in eleven nights, and on two of those nights there was no wind at all and there were still ripples, and they were moving toward the shore rather than along it.

I would like a second pair of eyes on that shoreline. Preferably eyes that aren't mine, because I have been looking at this for eleven nights and I have started to doubt them, and a Moon Guard who doubts his own observations should go and get somebody else's.
quests.turn_in_text: As I thought. Thank you for confirming what I'd begun to fear. I'll tell Maestra, and I'll sleep.

quests.title: Nets Full of Teeth
quests.description: Forty years, and the murlocs never touched a line.
quests.accept_text:
Forty years I've fished this strand. Forty.

In all that time the murlocs never touched a line of mine. We had an arrangement, near enough - they worked the shallows, I worked the deep, and if one of them got into the net he came out again and we both pretended it hadn't happened.

Now they're cutting my nets. With bone knives. Deliberately, from underneath, in the dark, and leaving the fish.

They're not hungry. That's the part that's had me awake. A hungry murloc takes the fish.

Deal with the spearfishers for me. And when you're back I'll tell you the story of the big silverfin, which is an extremely good story and which nobody on this coast will sit still for any more.
quests.turn_in_text: Ten! My boy, my nets will live. Now sit, sit, about the silverfin. It was longer than a dock and it winked.

quests.title: Cracked Traps
quests.description: Nothing is afraid of old Maelis any more.
quests.accept_text:
The crabs got bold when the naga started wandering the shallows.

That's the order it happened in and I'll stand by it. Naga came, everything else in the water had a worse thing to worry about than me, and now the big shore crabs take my traps and crush them against the rocks for no reason I can determine beyond that they can.

I've been rebuilding traps for a month. I'm an old man who spends his days making boxes for crabs to destroy, which was not the retirement I had sketched out.

Thin out the big ones. Then I'll be able to eat dinner like a free man instead of like a crab's tenant.
quests.turn_in_text: Eight. I can already smell the pot. You've done an old man a kindness, and kindness is rare on this coast.

quests.title: Splinters
quests.description: A boat takes a week to build and a night to sink.
quests.accept_text:
I build a boat in a week. They sink it in a night.

Three this month. Three, and I am most of the way through a fourth, and I have reached the point where I am building it slowly on purpose because finishing it means finding out whether it lasts till morning.

The coastguards come in off the reef after dark. They don't take anything and they don't come ashore. They hole the hulls and they go back out.

I'm not asking you to be brave about it. Bravery's no use to me - I've had brave, I had a nephew who was brave about it and I'd rather have had the boat and the nephew.

I'm asking you to be efficient. Drive them off the reef.
quests.turn_in_text: Eight. Hm. I'll build the fourth boat a little faster. You'll forgive me if I name it after you, I name them all after people who've been useful.

quests.title: Pearls of the Tide
quests.description: The tidecallers carry no weapons. They carry pearls.
quests.accept_text:
Here's the thing nobody at Zoram'gar will sit still long enough to hear.

The tidecallers don't carry weapons. Not one - I've been close enough to be sure of it, closer than I'd choose to be again.

They carry pearls, and the water answers them.

I build boats. That means I spend my life working out what water will do and planning around it, and I am telling you that water is not supposed to do what it does when one of those things holds a pearl up.

Bring some back. I want to know what a pearl is made of that it can do that, and whether it keeps doing it once it's out of a naga's hand. If it does, I can stop building boats that sink and start building ones that argue back.
quests.turn_in_text: These are not pearls. Nothing pearl-like should hum. I'm going to find out what they are, and I'm going to be very quiet about it.

quests.title: The Long Watch
quests.description: She watches the water so the others can sleep. She has not slept in days.
quests.accept_text:
I watch the water so the rest of them can sleep. That's the posting, and I've never resented it.

I watch the water and lately the water watches back. I know how that sounds. I have had several days to find a better way of saying it and that is still the most accurate one available.

Here's my actual problem, stripped of all that: I cannot see the Coast Bluffs from this post. There's a shoulder of rock in the way and there always has been, and for years that didn't matter.

I think that's where it's coming from. Go up there and walk them.

And if it's nothing - if it's birds and surf and a tired Sentinel - then come back and tell me that, and I will go to sleep for about a day and a half.
quests.turn_in_text: It isn't nothing. I'm grateful you told me anyway. Sit a while. The water will keep.

quests.title: The Quota
quests.description: Orgrimmar wants timber. The bears have other ideas.
quests.accept_text:
Orgrimmar wants timber. I want my loggers alive. For most of my career those have been the same objective and lately they have not been.

The grizzlies have decided the stand east of here is theirs. They come in at the crews, in daylight, which bears do not do unless something is very wrong with the arrangement they'd normally keep with us.

Deal with the biggest of them.

And before you suggest it - yes, I could send word to the Warchief and ask for the quota to be adjusted on account of bears. I'm told he's very reasonable about this sort of thing.

That is precisely why I am asking you instead.
quests.turn_in_text: Eight, and the quota's back on track. You're hired. Not formally. I don't do paperwork, but I'll remember your name.

quests.title: Orders in Blood
quests.description: Cultists never carry anything they can't hide behind a knife.
quests.accept_text:
Cultists carry orders. All of them do, and the Burning Blade are no exception - somebody has to tell them where to stand and when.

And a cultist never carries anything he can't hide behind a knife, which means the orders are ON them and they are small and they will be destroyed the moment one of them decides a fight is going badly.

So be quick about it. That's the whole of my tactical advice: be quick, and go through them before the ink has a chance to meet any blood.

Bring me the scraps. I don't care what the orders say - orders are always the same four sentences. I care about the HAND. Somebody is writing these, and a hand I can match is a person I can find.
quests.turn_in_text: Hm. Written in blood, signed in ash. Whoever's behind this wants to be found, eventually. I'd rather be ready.

quests.title: Wraiths in the Timber
quests.description: Sergeant Krull is tired of burying recruits.
quests.accept_text:
I have buried four recruits this week. FOUR. And they were four I trained myself, which I mention not for sympathy but so you understand I'm not reading this off a casualty list.

There are wraiths in the timber east of the post. They come at the woodcutting details and the details are exactly the wrong people to meet them - axes, no shields, and half of them are nineteen.

I want them back in the dirt.

And don't. Don't say it. I have had three separate people explain to me this week that they're already dead, as though that were a clever observation that had not occurred to me, and the next one who says it is digging the graves.
quests.turn_in_text: Seven? SEVEN. I can't say good job in front of the recruits so I'll say it here. Good job.

quests.title: Eyes on the Wastes
quests.description: From the wall he sees smoke. From the ground you see who lit it.
quests.accept_text:
From this wall, I see smoke. Every night, from somewhere out in the Wastes, and I have logged the position of it the best I can from up here.

From the ground, you see who lit it.

That's the whole difference between my job and the job I'm asking you to do, and I'd swap if I could - but if I come off this wall there is nobody on it, and a wall with nobody on it is a fence.

Walk the edge of the Wastes and come back and tell me what's burning and who's standing round it.

I'll keep the wall warm. That's a joke. It's the only one I've got and I've been working on it for two weeks.
quests.turn_in_text: Hm. Smoke without a fire, you say? Some things burn the other way. I'll tell Gorada. He'll curse a lot.

quests.title: Remnants
quests.description: Not alive, not dead, and not made for the world.
quests.accept_text:
The remnants drift through the Wastes after dark.

They're not alive. They're not dead either, and I've had that argument with a priest and won it. They're not MADE for the world - that's the nearest I can get. Something summoned them here and then stopped paying attention, and they've been bumping along the inside of a place that doesn't want them ever since.

They're drifting closer to the wall every night. I've marked it.

Disperse them out there, before they get close enough to find out how thin this wall actually is. I know how thin it is. I'd prefer to keep that between us.
quests.turn_in_text: Six. The wall is quiet. I'll sleep tonight, which is more than I can say for the Wastes.

quests.title: Felling Season
quests.description: A good tree dies in four swings. These take it back.
quests.accept_text:
A good tree dies in four swings. Four. I've timed it, I've trained it, and I've built a camp's whole work rate around it.

These walkers take it back with a root in the ear.

The timberlings stand with the stand east of camp and they don't let a crew near it - and they're patient about it, they don't charge, they just put themselves between my boys and the trunk until somebody loses their temper and then it's a funeral.

Clear them off so my crews can work.

And don't leave any standing. I've tried leaving a few. They fetch more.
quests.turn_in_text: Eight. I owe you a few logs' worth of thanks. Take your pick of the leftover axes. They're not good, but they're mine.

quests.title: The Elder Stump
quests.description: There's a stump out there that walks.
quests.accept_text:
There's a stump out there that walks.

I've cut forty years of trees. I've taken things down that were old when my grandfather's clan came over the sea, and I've never minded it - a tree's a tree and a camp's a camp and I sleep like a stone.

That one's the oldest thing in this forest and it guards the last good stand, and I have never in my life wanted something gone so badly.

I'm not going to dress that up as duty. It's the quota, and it's also that it stood and looked at me across the cut for an hour last week and I've not slept right since.

Fell it. The camp will drink to it and I'll be buying.
quests.turn_in_text: It fell? It FELL! Hah! The whole camp will hear about this. Take the sap, it's good for something, I'm sure.

quests.title: Silk for the Slings
quests.description: Rope breaks. Silk doesn't.
quests.accept_text:
Rope breaks. That's not a complaint, it's an engineering fact, and every log-sling in this camp is rope and every one of them will eventually part under a full oak.

Silk doesn't.

The forest spiders out here are bigger than they have any business being, and so is their silk - the strands come off them thick as a bootlace and you cannot cut one with a belt knife, I've tried in front of witnesses.

Bring me bundles of it. Enough to weave slings with.

I'll lift a whole oak in one piece and I'll do it in front of the Overseer, who has been telling me for two years that it can't be done with the crew I've got.
quests.turn_in_text: Six, and clean. Look at that, it doesn't even stretch. I'll make you a sling of your own. For a bear. Or a friend you hate.

quests.title: Cats at the Door
quests.description: She does not welcome strangers. The cats don't distinguish either.
quests.accept_text:
I do not generally welcome strangers to this retreat. I certainly do not generally welcome the Horde, and I'd rather say so to your face than have you find it out in my manner.

The nightsabers don't distinguish.

They've stopped respecting the quiet here. Raynewood has kept a boundary for a very long time without a fence - the cats knew where it was and they kept to the other side of it, and now they come through it at dusk and they come as far as the door.

Drive them off.

When it's done the retreat can go back to being quiet, and you and I can go back to our respective positions on each other, which I think we'd both prefer.
quests.turn_in_text: Seven. The retreat is quiet. I will say a thing I haven't said to a stranger in years: thank you.

quests.title: Vigil Lights
quests.description: We light a vigil for the ones the forest lost.
quests.accept_text:
We keep a vigil here for the ones the forest has lost. Not the fallen - the LOST, which is a different list and a longer one: the ones who went into the corruption and did not come out and were never found to be buried.

It's lit with wisp-light. It has been since before Raynewood had a roof.

The wisps give it freely, if you ask them. That is the entire method and I am aware of how it sounds to somebody who arrived this morning with an axe.

So ask. Stand still, and ask, and take what they let fall.

If you take one that wasn't offered the vigil will still light. It simply won't mean anything, and I would be the only one who knew, and I'd know for years.
quests.turn_in_text: Six. That will see us through the new moon. Walk carefully out there. I'd rather not add you to the vigil.

quests.title: The Dryads Sleep
quests.description: They sleep, and what wakes in them is not them.
quests.accept_text:
The dryads here have gone to sleep. That by itself would be no cause for alarm - they do sleep, deeply, for longer than you'd credit.

What wakes in them is not them.

I've watched it happen twice now. The sleep goes on too long, and then there's movement, and what gets up moves wrong from the first step. There is nothing of the dryad left in it by the time it's standing.

Put them to rest rather than leave them to that. I'd do it myself - I want that said - but my hands are not what they used to be and this is not work to do badly.

Quickly, please. And not while they're still sleeping, if you can help it. Let them be asleep.
quests.turn_in_text: I will light a candle for each. Thank you for doing what I could not. It will be remembered at Raynewood.
